key_insight: Encoding conditions in input states lets a shared IQP Born machine represent conditional families inaccessible to diagonal conditioning at the same qubit count.
engineering_relevance: This approach enables classical training of conditional quantum generative models without requiring quantum hardware during optimization.
method: Encode each condition in the input state and share one IQP unitary across conditions.
Use efficient reference-state sampling and amplitude-ratio evaluation to estimate a conditional maximum mean discrepancy objective.
Train with unbiased classical estimates of the objective and its gradients.
evidence_signal: On the 16-qubit Curie–Weiss model, mean total variation distance was six times lower than diagonal conditioning at held-out temperatures; models up to 2048 qubits reproduced mean squared magnetization away from the crossover.
watch_item: Efficient training depends on tractable reference-state sampling and amplitude-ratio evaluation; the reported scaling does not establish quantum advantage.
paper_title: Classical training of conditional instantaneous quantum polynomial-time Born machines
